newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-DE FERRAN SNAPS ZANARDI'S POLE STREAK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-DE FERRAN SNAPS ZANARDI'S POLE STREAK.

text.p: Brazilian Gil de Ferran snapped Italian Alessandro Zanardi's six-race pole streak without a single tour of the Long Beach circuit on Saturday.

De Ferran, who held provisional pole after Friday qualifying for Sunday's Long Beach Grand Prix CART race, sat in the pits in his back-up Reynard Honda after wrecking his primary car during morning practice.
But his fastest Friday time of 51.293 seconds held up despite a frustrating afternoon of inaction for the Brazilian.

"It was very difficult to sit in the car and not run," de Ferran said. "You have control of your destiny when you are out on the track running. In this situation I felt completely helpless. I just had to sit and wait."
The long wait paid off in de Ferran's third career pole. He also started from pole here last year.
The accident happened when Brazilian rookie Gualter Salles stalled his car at the end of the straight on Shoreline Drive.
"I was rapidly closing in on Hiro (Matsushita) when he moved from the lower line up towards the wall," de Ferran recalled. "As he cleared my line of sight, Salles's car was directly in front of me.

"There was insufficient time for me to avoid him," added de Ferran, who was able to turn his wheel just enough to avoid a head-on collision "by a millimetre." But the impact sheered the left side wheels off of his car.

Zanardi, who improved his time to 51.665 seconds on the 2.56 kilometre street circuit in his Reynard Honda, had to settle for second after damaging his car in a spin with 10 minutes left in the session.
"My car was better today," said Zanardi, who will still start from the front row for the record 11th consecutive race despite missing the pole.
"If I had another lap I would have won the pole," said the 1996 CART Rookie of the Year.

Mauricio Gugelmin of Brazil dropped from second to third on the grid in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz at 51.745, followed by last week's winner in Australia, Scott Pruett, who recorded a time of 51.795 in a Reynard Ford.
Michael Andretti, winner of the season opener at Homestead, Florida, will start fifth in the 27-car field for the 105-lap race.
